plan.status: Proposed. Agree it with the group and commit it before the first real run; do not edit it after seeing any result.
plan.design: Each method is trained twice per seed: the unchanged published control and the same run with FedLC. Within a seed both arms share initialization, client partition, sampled rows, learning rate and work. Only the training loss changes.
plan.loss_choice: FedLC calibrates logits before the frozen fixed-training-mean sqrt-weighted CE, so the controls are exactly the published runs. Stacking FedLC on class weights may correct imbalance twice; a separate plan with base_loss 'ce' tests FedLC on ordinary CE against an ordinary-CE control.
plan.fedlc_rule: Client c trains on z_j - tau * max(n_cj, count_floor)**(-1/4), with n_cj its fit-population count of class j in raw rows. tau=1 follows the authors' default and is not tuned here. Inference uses unadjusted logits.
plan.evaluation: Final endpoints only, on development data. Reuse the published grouped calibration/audit split and strict-margin order-statistic thresholds; fit each threshold on calibration benign rows, then score the audit half once. Report all four targets; assess at the 5% target. No threshold, checkpoint, tau or seed selection.
plan.decision: A method supports FedLC only if, at the 5% target, every seed keeps macro-F1 within 0.01 of its control, actual FAR within 0.5 points, and every non-target class recall within 5 points; and, averaged over seeds, the mean recall of Web-based/Brute Force/Spoofing rises by at least 2 points with no fall in their mean F1. These are new proposed engineering targets, not existing project gates.
plan.limits: Previously examined development data, one fixed 20-client non-IID partition and three training seeds. No confirmation, original validation or test scoring. Not a new capture-session generalization, privacy, edge or deployment result.
